If you're thinking about getting a folding bike to avoid having your bike stolen, then this post may be of interest to you.

In 2 words: it's awesome. Apparently it's true what they say: small wheels really are great for hill climbing. I went with 20'' wheels and 1.75" wide tires, a 1x7 drivetrain, and with the whole bike weighing less than 26 pounds. To that, I added a set of panniers on the rear rack, installed a front rack, and then took it out for some light shopping. Despite only having 7 gears, it climbs great, but I obviously expect that there are limits to this when compared to my touring bike. Even though the touring bike is much heavier, it has way more gears for climbing.

So how fast is it? While it accelerates a little quicker from a stop due to the small wheels, let's just say that you aren't going to win any races with it. It tops out pretty quickly. I found myself cruising (low to medium effort) between 12-15 mph over variable terrain, which I guess isn't too bad. On the flats, you can get it up to 20 mph with some effort, but going faster becomes more trouble than it's worth. It's a very upright bike, as most folders are. You can't get into an aero position, so air drag becomes a major problem. I doubt I could get it going much faster than 25 mph, but you wouldn't want to. Because of the small wheels, the steering is very twitchy, especially at high speeds. It takes a bit of getting used to.

So far the bike feels nice and stiff, but that will probably change with time. The ride is smooth, but that's probably due to my tire width, plus I opted not to pump them up to maximum pressure. I don't think skinny or high pressure tires would be good for the hinges. Basically my thinking is that the softer the ride, the less wear I'll have on the bike. Maybe that's wrong, but it seems right.

So overall, I'm pretty impressed. The bike rides well, and it's enjoyable. It forces you to ride in a much more relaxed manner, which is kind of nice for a change, and it's not bad at climbing, even with only 7 gears. Inexperienced riders would probably want more gears though. I've got fairly good legs at this point, and I'm also very used to climbing hills, so YMMV.
